data.executive_summary: Middle East conflict continues to intensify, with reported Israeli strikes in south Lebanon and US-Iran escalation indicators, while Tehran links Islamabad talks to specific terms. Market and policy signals in Pakistan show heightened sensitivity to regional shocks, including reported erosion of T-bill investment and fuel-supply stress headlines tied to the war. Domestically, the government is rolling out relief funds via digital wallets amid inflation at 7.30% YoY (March 2026) and a KSE-100 session decline of 1.06% on Apr 03. Weather-related fatalities in KP and Punjab and governance/service delivery criticisms in Sindh add to internal pressure points.
key_takeaways: Regional escalation dominated: reports include Israeli strikes hitting a hospital and homes in south Lebanon and continued US-Iran conflict updates.
Tehran stated Islamabad talks depend on terms, indicating conditionality in Pakistan-Iran engagement.
Balochistan fixed the price of Iranian petrol at Rs280, reflecting provincial-level management of cross-border fuel dynamics.
Pakistan’s foreign office rejected claims regarding UAE debt repayment, characterizing it as a routine financial transaction.
Government initiated relief disbursements through digital wallets, positioning social support delivery as a near-term priority.
economic_watch: KSE-100 closed down 1.06% at 150,398.71 (Apr 03), aligning with risk-off sentiment amid regional conflict headlines.
CPI stood at 7.30% YoY and 1.20% MoM in March 2026, keeping cost-of-living pressures elevated.
Remittances were $3,287.86M in Feb 2026, down 5.10% MoM, while forex reserves rose to $21,331.86M (+1.24% MoM).
External sector remained mixed: current account was $427.00M (Feb 2026) with imports $6,062.00M (-6.65% MoM) and exports $3,293.00M (-9.13% MoM).
FDI increased to $213.52M (+23.22% MoM) in Feb 2026, while government debt rose to ₨79,322.41B (+1.01% MoM) in Jan 2026.
A Dawn report cited Gulf war impacts eroding 90% investment in T-bills, signaling stress in domestic fixed-income positioning.
risks: Regional conflict risk remains acute, with reported strikes in Lebanon and escalatory rhetoric and operational updates in the US-Iran war stream.
Energy supply and pricing pressures are highlighted by war-linked fuel-supply constraints and Balochistan’s administered pricing for Iranian petrol.
Information environment constraints increased as a US satellite firm announced a blackout on war-on-Iran images, reducing open-source imagery availability.
Domestic stability risk includes weather-related deaths in KP and Punjab with additional rainfall spells forecast.
Governance and service delivery concerns surfaced with criticism that SSWMB has failed to deliver and concerns raised over rules tied to Sindh Women Agri Workers’ Act 2019.
watchlist: Pakistan-Iran engagement signals following Tehran’s statement that Islamabad talks depend on terms and ongoing regional escalation.
Developments around Strait of Hormuz transit levels after Iran said Iraqi ships can pass as transits tick up.
Domestic market reactions to conflict-linked financial stress, including reported T-bill investment erosion and equity weakness.
Fuel pricing and policy debate, including calls for fuel price deregulation and provincial measures on Iranian petrol pricing.
Security and law-and-order indicators including the Houston killing of Dr. Aafia Siddiqui’s nephew and high-profile judicial activity in the Noor Mukadam case review hearing on April 8.
Civil-military and capability signaling after the Navy inducted an advanced corvette.

highlights: Pakistan approved diversion of surplus LNG cargoes under Qatar contracts for FY26.
Long-term LNG agreements remain the backbone of energy ties.
A $3B investment protocol was formalized through the Joint Ministerial Commission.

notes: Work visas remain significant for Pakistani expatriates.
Visit visas require sponsor approvals.

countries.name: Kuwait
countries.recent_visit: Phone call with Crown Prince Sheikh Sabah, Mar 2026; no PM visit in 2025
highlights: Kuwait Fund financing continues for the Mohmand Dam hydropower project.
Kuwait Investment Authority exploring expanded portfolio in Pakistan.
Bilateral business expos and trade consultations remain active.

notes: Labor migration continues under sponsor-based system.
Visit visa issuance subject to compliance checks.

countries.name: Bahrain
countries.recent_visit: PM Sharif visited Bahrain, Nov 2025
highlights: High-level visits in late 2025 and early 2026 aimed to lift trade to $1B.
Defense cooperation and training ties were reaffirmed.
Bilateral agenda includes IT, healthcare, energy, and logistics.

notes: Work visas remain available for skilled labor categories.
Visit visas require sponsor and compliance checks.

countries.name: Oman
countries.recent_visit: Naval chief visited Oman, Dec 2025; MoU signed
highlights: Energy cooperation includes regular petroleum cargo imports from Oman.
Naval MoU signed for maritime information sharing and cooperation.
Diplomatic engagement continues across energy and security.

notes: Work visas continue for Pakistani nationals in energy and services.
Visit visas require sponsor approval.

countries.name: United States
countries.recent_visit: Army Chief FM Asim Munir visited Washington, Jun 2025; met President Trump. Second visit Aug 2025 at CENTCOM
highlights: Joint counterterrorism operations and intelligence exchanges expanded in 2025.
Military engagement and security dialogue revived after Afghanistan drawdown.
Defense cooperation includes F-16 sustainment and strategic minerals discussions.

notes: Nonimmigrant visas require interviews and security vetting.
Student and work visas remain active with compliance checks.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.recent_visit: PM Sharif visited London, Sep 2025; met UK officials and diaspora
highlights: Pakistan-UK Trade Dialogue Mechanism launched in 2025 with sectoral working groups.
Both sides exploring a future FTA and services cooperation.
Trade volumes exceed £5.5B with emphasis on IT, agriculture, education.

notes: Standard visitor and student visas require biometric checks.
Seasonal worker routes remain limited.

countries.name: Russia
countries.recent_visit: PM Sharif met Putin at SCO sidelines in China, Sep 2025
highlights: Pakistan Stream gas pipeline project discussions continue.
PM Sharif met President Putin on SCO sidelines in Jul 2025.
Bilateral trade remains modest but energy cooperation is expanding.

notes: Visa required; processing through Moscow embassy.
Business and diplomatic visas require invitation letters.

countries.name: Turkey
countries.recent_visit: PM Sharif met President Erdogan on SCO sidelines, Jul 2025
highlights: Turkey is among Pakistan's most consistent supporters on the Kashmir issue at the UN.
Defense cooperation expanded; Pakistan operates Bayraktar TB2 drones and military tech agreements are ongoing.
PM Sharif and President Erdogan held bilateral talks on trade, defence, and regional security in 2025.
Bilateral trade target set at $5B; both sides pursuing FTA negotiations.
Cultural and religious ties remain deep with high-level exchanges and diaspora links.

notes: Pakistani nationals can obtain visa on arrival for 30 days.
E-visa also available for tourism and business travel.

countries.name: Azerbaijan
countries.recent_visit: PM Sharif visited Baku, Nov 2025 (5+ visits in 2025); $2B investment pledge
highlights: Five PM visits in 2025 underscore deep strategic alignment.
Trade agreements and business forums expanded bilateral commerce.
Defense cooperation and mutual political support remain strong.

notes: E-visa available for Pakistani nationals via ASAN Visa.
Business and tourist visas processed within days.

sources.title: MOFA: PM visit to Azerbaijan Feb 2025

countries.name: Tajikistan
countries.recent_visit: PM Sharif visited Dushanbe, May 2025; met President Rahmon
highlights: PM Sharif visited Dushanbe Jul 2025 to strengthen trade and connectivity.
CASA-1000 power transmission project links both countries.
Transit trade and cross-border connectivity remain key agenda items.

notes: Visa required; processing through Dushanbe embassy.
Facilitated visas for business and official travel.

countries.name: Kazakhstan
countries.recent_visit: No confirmed PM visit in 2025; SCO Summit was held in China
highlights: PM Sharif attended SCO Summit in Astana Jul 2025.
Energy and transit trade cooperation discussed bilaterally.
Kazakhstan is a key partner in Central Asian connectivity.

notes: Visa required; processing through Astana embassy.
Business visas available with invitation letters.

highlights: EU GSP+ preferences extended through 2027; monitoring continues on reforms.
Textiles remain the largest beneficiary of preferential access.
EU-Pakistan Joint Commission in 2025 reaffirmed the partnership.

notes: Schengen visas required for most EU destinations.
Processing times vary by consulate.

Business chambers continue sectoral engagements in energy and manufacturing.
Development cooperation focuses on energy transition and skills.

notes: Schengen visa required; appointments often backlogged.
Business and study visas require documentation.

Port and logistics cooperation discussions continue.
Dutch import demand remains strong for textiles and agriculture.

Business travel requires invitation documentation.

Bilateral cultural and education ties continue alongside trade.
